page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on the x86_64 CPU architecture. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs alongside 128 GB of system memory, matching a standard ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance contains no hardware accelerators, with a GPU count of zero, directing all resources toward general compute tasks.

The virtual machine does not come with integrated local disk storage, meaning persistent data storage relies on attached network volumes. Additionally, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses upon deployment. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures dedicated compute capacity across all 32 vCPUs without contention from other tenant workloads on the host hypervisor.

With its 1:4 compute-to-memory profile, the n4d-standard-32 delivers a balanced resource distribution suited for enterprise middle-tier backends, relational databases utilizing cloud disks, containerized application clusters, and multi-threaded compilation pipelines that do not depend on specialized vector or GPU acceleration.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine offering 32 dedicated vCPUs and 128 GB of RAM on the x86_64 architecture. Built around a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per core), it provides consistent resource allocation for scalable multi-threaded operations. The instance features no bundled local disk storage and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring network storage attachments for persistent state. It does not include GPU accelerators, prioritizing standard compute and memory throughput. The dedicated CPU configuration avoids hypervisor thread contention, making the instance a practical choice for running enterprise application servers, container nodes, relational databases, and multi-core batch processing pipelines.
